text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV:P1 — Elevated 5xx rate observed from prod-gateway (edge) starting ~07:12 UTC. Auto-page: @oncall-sre. Aggregated alarm: gateway-5xx-rate > 2% sustained for 3m.

oncall-sre: acked. I'm on it, will triage.

maria: seeing a lot of 502 and 504 in the gateway logs. Example tail: 
```
[07:14:02] GET /v1/generate 502 svc=frontend-backend err="upstream reset" host=gateway-prod-1
[07:14:03] GET /v1/embeds 504 svc=model-proxy err="timeout waiting for response"
```
No consistent request-id present in those lines. Trace sampling is currently 1%.

jonathan: traffic spike? metrics show qps ~1.6x baseline but not huge. Error rate correlates with requests hitting model-proxy pods that report elevated CPU and some OOMKill events earlier in the morning.

priya: customer reports: 4 enterprise orgs showing increased failures in synthetic checks. Support says partial failures, some retries succeed. Impact estimate: ~3% of total requests, but higher for long-running generate endpoints.

maria: quick plan: 1) add stopgap logging to edge to surface request-id and trace ids for failed requests 2) increase trace sampling to 100% for 15m 3) route a small % of traffic away from model-proxy to warm standby region if backend continues to fail.

oncall-sre: agree. I'm going to flip two quick things now: bump gateway replicas by 2 and enable debug request logging at edge. Executing.

oncall-sre: command run: 
```
kubectl -n gateway scale deploy/gateway-prod --replicas=8
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/configs/gateway/logging" -d '{"level":"debug","sample_failed":true}'
```

maria: also enabling trace sampling: 
```
curl -X PATCH "https://tracing.internal/sampling" -d '{"service":"gateway-prod","sample_rate":1.0}'
```

jonathan: enabling 100% sampling now. hooking up temporary log-forwarder to S3 for heavy-failed requests. Will also add an X-Request-ID injector middleware as stopgap to ensure correlation.

priya: can we add a simple middleware patch rather than full deploy? A small patch to the gateway config to set header if missing. Suggestion: Envoy lua filter to inject `x-request-id` when absent. Example: 
```
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local id = request_handle:headers():get("x-request-id")
        if not id then
          request_handle:headers():add("x-request-id", os.time().."-tmp")
        end
      end
```

oncall-sre: applying lua filter as a hot reload. Pushing to prod-edge config now.

support-ops-bot: Noted — sending proactive message to affected customers list and opening a status page incident banner: "Some requests may fail with 502/504; engineering is investigating."

maria: important: observability gap summary — missing request ids + 1% trace sampling earlier meant we couldn't correlate failing requests to backend pods. That's why we couldn't quickly identify the OOMKill pattern in model-proxy. The stopgap inject+sampling should let us link logs -> traces -> pods.

jonathan: initial mitigation results: after scaling and enabling debug logs, 5xx rate dropped from 2.5% -> 0.8% over 6m. Some residual 504s remain for long streaming requests.

maria: mitigation checklist for handoff to next oncall (to be done before I sign off):
- Ensure lua injector is active and logs are flowing to S3 (jonathan)
- Keep trace sampling at 100% for next 20m, then drop to 10% if stable (maria)
- Monitor model-proxy pod events for OOMKill — increase limits or roll a stable image if repeated (priya)
- Route 15% traffic to secondary region as fallback if errors >1% in next 10m (oncall-sre)
- Update status page with "reducing impact" message and note ETA for deeper RCA (support-ops-bot)

lee: taking handoff at 07:35 UTC — I'll own the follow-up and RCA. My immediate items: verify S3 log objects contain x-request-id and matching trace ids, check model-proxy memory footprints across recent restarts, and validate canary routing tests before rerouting more traffic.

oncall-sre: assigning runbook tasks: runbook/pg-gateway -> section "5xx spike - trace deficit" steps 1-6 applied. Leaving note in runbook: temporarily increased sampling and added lua injector (remove after RCA).

priya: note on customer impact: 4 enterprise customers on Dedicated may have seen higher failure rates due to pinned model-proxy instances on same node pool. I'm opening a customer-impact thread to ops to prepare playbooks for each org.

maria: quick logs excerpt after injector live: 
```
[07:23:10] GET /v1/generate 502 x-request-id=2481234567-abc trace_id=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00 span_id=00 svc=model-proxy err="upstream reset"
```
Now we can see trace_id -> span -> pod. Good.

jonathan: plan for next 2 hours: 1) keep sampling high for correlation 2) collect heap profiles from model-proxy pods that restarted 3) if OOMs confirmed, roll resource bump + image with patched memory leak.

lee: updating oncall notes and will add checklist for reverting lua injector and sampling change once RCA complete. I'll escalate to platform if we need longer-term telemetry changes (e.g., permanent 0.5% higher sampling or ensure request-id generation upstream).

support-ops-bot: status page updated to "under mitigation". Customer comms draft posted to #customer-notifications for review.

maria: summary: root cause likely model-proxy memory pressure causing resets -> gateway 502/504. Observability gap (no request-id + low sampling) slowed triage. Stopgaps: lua injector, 100% sampling, scale up gateway, route fallback. Result: error rate falling but remaintingly elevated for streaming endpoints. Handoff to @lee for 2hr follow-up and RCA.

oncall-sre: closing pager for now — leave elevated-monitoring channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:

lee: taking over. Please DM me any extra context.

(ends)
